nodes.label: URL Ingest (/graphify add)
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects YouTube, Twitter/X, arXiv, PDF, image and generic webpage URLs, saves to ./raw with author/contributor provenance, then runs --update to merge into the existing graph.

nodes.label: FalkorDB Export
nodes.rationale: Statements are OpenCypher, but FalkorDB's GRAPH.QUERY runs one statement at a time with no bulk script import, so --falkordb-push is preferred over the portable cypher.txt artifact.

nodes.label: Graphify MCP Server
nodes.rationale: Exposes query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats and shortest_path over stdio so other agents can query the graph live. Claude Desktop cannot run $(...), so the absolute interpreter path must be used.

nodes.label: Neo4j Export
nodes.rationale: Uses MERGE so re-running never creates duplicates.

nodes.label: Wiki Export
nodes.rationale: Must run before Step 9 cleanup so .graphify_labels.json still exists.

nodes.label: Hyperedges
nodes.rationale: Used only when 3+ nodes share a concept that pairwise edges cannot express; capped at 3 per chunk to keep them informative.

nodes.label: GitHub Repo Clone
nodes.rationale: Clones into ~/.graphify/repos/<owner>/<repo> and reuses existing clones on repeat runs.

nodes.label: Native CLAUDE.md Integration
nodes.rationale: `graphify claude install` writes a ## graphify section into the project CLAUDE.md so the graph is consulted automatically in future sessions with no manual /graphify.

nodes.label: BFS and DFS Traversal Modes
nodes.rationale: BFS answers 'what is X connected to' with layered neighbors to depth 3; DFS traces 'how does X reach Y' depth-limited to 6 so it does not walk the whole graph.

nodes.label: Query Token Budget
nodes.rationale: Output is ranked by term overlap then truncated at ~4 chars/token so the most relevant nodes survive the cut.

nodes.label: Whisper Domain Hint Prompt
nodes.rationale: A one-sentence domain hint derived from existing god nodes improves transcription accuracy on jargon; a video-only corpus falls back to a generic punctuation prompt.

nodes.label: Community Labeling
nodes.rationale: Communities are re-exported with curated names (#2490) so graph.json nodes carry community_name, and questions are regenerated after labeling because labels affect question phrasing.

nodes.label: Folder Watcher (--watch)
nodes.rationale: Code changes rebuild automatically because AST needs no LLM; doc/paper/image changes only raise a needs_update flag because they require paid semantic re-extraction. A 3s debounce prevents a wave of parallel agent writes from triggering a rebuild per file.

nodes.label: Verbatim source_file Rule
nodes.rationale: Copying the FILE_LIST path character-for-character keeps full builds and incremental --update on the same base, so build_merge's replace-on-re-extract matches the existing node instead of accumulating duplicates.

nodes.label: Cross-Repo Graph Merge
nodes.rationale: The skill pipeline always writes to graphify-out/ in cwd, so running it per subfolder would clobber the same output dir; the CLI is used per subfolder instead (it nests graphify-out/ inside each scanned path) and merge-graphs combines them. Each merged node carries a `repo` attribute for filtering.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Auto-Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit instead of running a background process, works with any editor, and appends to an existing post-commit hook rather than replacing it. Only code changes are handled; docs need a manual --update.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Expansion
nodes.rationale: The query CLI matches by case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming, synonyms or cross-language mapping, so a wording mismatch returns zero hits. Expansion is constrained to tokens actually present in graph.json node labels to prevent fabricating a search.

nodes.label: Work Memory Self-Improving Loop
nodes.rationale: save-result with --outcome useful|dead_end|corrected feeds LESSONS.md, so later sessions start from preferred sources, skip known dead ends, and see prior corrections; `reflect --if-stale` keeps it cheap and deterministic.

nodes.label: Whisper Transcription
nodes.rationale: Video and audio cannot be read directly, so they are transcribed to text and then treated as documents. The host agent writes the Whisper initial prompt itself from god-node labels — it is already a language model, so no extra API call is needed.

nodes.label: build_merge Replace-on-Re-extract
nodes.rationale: build_merge reads graph.json directly with no NetworkX round-trip so edge direction survives (#801). prune_sources is only for genuinely deleted files — adding changed files there would delete the freshly re-extracted content (#1344/#1178), and root= is required or nothing is pruned and stale nodes accumulate (#1361).

nodes.label: Cluster-Only Rerun
nodes.rationale: `graphify cluster-only .` is self-contained; re-running Steps 5-9 afterwards raises FileNotFoundError because Step 9 cleanup already deleted the intermediate sidecars (#1392).

nodes.label: Code-Only Update Shortcut
nodes.rationale: If every changed file has a code extension, semantic extraction is skipped entirely — AST alone is sufficient and costs no tokens.

nodes.label: Incremental Update (--update)
nodes.rationale: Re-extracts only new or changed files to save tokens. `files` carries the changed subset while `all_files` carries the full corpus so later steps still see corpus-wide context.

nodes.label: AST Structural Extraction (Part A)
nodes.rationale: Code is extracted deterministically with no LLM and no API key, which makes a code-only corpus free; it also means graphify never needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and must never block on one.

nodes.label: Fast Path For Existing Graph
nodes.rationale: When graphify-out/graph.json already exists, rebuilding to answer a natural-language question wastes tokens and time; the graph is already the answer surface, so Steps 1-5 are skipped entirely and `graphify query` runs immediately.

nodes.label: Manifest Stamping
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped (#2015) — stamping a doc whose chunk failed would mark it done and lose its content forever. Dispatched-but-unstamped files get their semantic_hash cleared (#1948), and manifest keys are relativized to the scan root so they stay portable across clones (#1417).

nodes.label: No API Key Required
nodes.rationale: Only GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY are ever read; absent those the host agent itself is the LLM. Prompting for ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or any other provider key is explicitly a misread of the skill.

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction (Part B)
nodes.rationale: Only docs, papers and images need LLM extraction. Subagents must be general-purpose (not Explore) because Explore is read-only and would silently drop chunk files; all subagents are dispatched in one message so they run in parallel.

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction Cache
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are stamped with the SPEC_PATH prompt that produced them (#1939), so a prompt upgrade invalidates stale entries instead of replaying them; the cached file is deleted when empty so Part C never merges a stale .graphify_cached.json (#1392).

nodes.label: graph.json Shrink Guard
nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to write a graph smaller than the existing one (#479) so a failed extraction cannot clobber a good graph; GRAPH_REPORT.md and the analysis sidecar are only written after the export succeeds so they never describe a graph graph.json does not contain (#1392).

nodes.label: Token Reduction Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Only run above 5,000 words — for small corpora the graph's value is structural clarity, not token compression.

nodes.label: EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Uncertain relationships are flagged rather than omitted, so the graph records what it does not know instead of quietly dropping it.

nodes.label: Expense Tracker API Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Only POST /budgets/crt and POST /expenses/crt exist under /api/v1/expense_tracker; read, update and delete are not built and category CRUD is deferred because the 7 seeded categories cover normal use.

nodes.label: Expense Tracker Category
nodes.rationale: Categories are global reference data with 7 seeded rows and no CRUD yet; deleting one is RESTRICTed while anything references it.

nodes.label: Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: A discrete five-value set (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) replaces a continuous range because models collapse ranges to a binary — production showed >50% of edges at 0.5 and >40% at 0.85+.

nodes.label: Node ID Format
nodes.rationale: IDs must be the full repo-relative path stem plus entity so same-named files in different directories stay distinct and the LLM id matches the AST id exactly; using only the filename or immediate parent, or appending chunk suffixes, creates orphan ghost-duplicate nodes.

nodes.label: Graph Health Check
nodes.rationale: Read-only gate that surfaces dangling, missing, self-loop and collapsed edges — the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches. It never aborts because the graph is still usable, but the Honesty Rules require the issue be visible.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS), never skip the corpus warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion behind symbols, never visualize >5000 nodes without warning — the audit trail is the product's credibility.

nodes.label: Python Interpreter Resolution
nodes.rationale: uv tool, pipx, venv and system installs each put graphify under a different interpreter, so the resolved path is persisted to graphify-out/.graphify_python and every later block substitutes it for python3.

nodes.label: BaseEntity Timestamp Stripping
nodes.rationale: created_at, updated_at (trigger-maintained) and deleted_at (soft delete) are stripped from every client payload by BaseEntity so they can never be set from a request body.

nodes.label: _budget Response Envelope
nodes.rationale: The created expense echoes a _budget object naming which pot it landed in, or null when unbudgeted — without it the server-side resolution would be invisible to the caller.

nodes.label: currentUser Identity Seam
nodes.rationale: src/middleware/currentUser.js resolves every request to the seeded dev user (id 1) and is deliberately the only place identity is decided — controllers pass req.user.id down and every query filters on user_id, so shipping real auth means replacing exactly one file.

nodes.label: Duplicate Expense Detection
nodes.rationale: Same title + amount + date within 5 minutes attaches a _warning but still succeeds — a legitimate repeat purchase must not be blocked, so detection warns rather than rejects.

nodes.label: Envelope Budgeting
nodes.rationale: A budget is a named pot with a fixed start_date/end_date window and no recurring cadence; a monthly rhythm is many budgets, one per month. Dropping recurrence is what makes drawdown a single SUM.

nodes.label: Migration 004 Deliberate Removals
nodes.rationale: Tags, the expense-tag junction, payment methods, is_recurring and budget `period` were dropped because each was unreferenced or ambiguous; budget `period` in particular made drawdown unresolvable since summing expenses against a recurring rule spans every period at once.

nodes.label: One Budget Per Scope Per Window
nodes.norm_label: one budget per scope per window
nodes.rationale: Overlapping budgets for the same scope are rejected at create time with 409. Enforcing uniqueness at write time makes budget resolution unambiguous and 'what's left' a single SUM at read time.

nodes.label: Ownership Filtering
nodes.rationale: Ownership is always taken from req.user.id; a user_id supplied in a request body is rejected outright.

nodes.label: Raw SQL Queries Layer
nodes.rationale: Raw SQL over the shared pg Pool from src/config/db.js with no ORM, and all SQL confined to *.queries.js files — never a service or controller — so ownership filtering has exactly one layer to audit.

nodes.label: Server-Side Budget Resolution
nodes.rationale: Clients never send budget_id; the server derives it from category and date so resolution cannot be spoofed or drift. Category-specific budgets beat overall ones so groceries hit the Food pot rather than the catch-all.

nodes.label: Unbudgeted Expense (budget_id null)
nodes.rationale: Spending no budget covers is still recorded with budget_id = null, because refusing to log real spending would be worse than leaving it unbudgeted.
